about: Signature behaviours of the water (sig2-aquatic, AnimalDex docs/ark/signature-behaviours.json, decision 367/369): the species whose own stored sentence has them act with another kind of the Ark (a cleaner at a larger swimmer, a moray with a grouper, a surgeonfish with other surgeonfishes) or with its mate (an angelfish pair). `with` says who, from that sentence: `larger` any water animal that many times its length; `slugs` those species; `pattern` a slug pattern (the family the sentence names); `same` its own kind. `stage` gates the acts the sentence gives to the young or the adults only. `block` is what the act shows once it is there. Each row keeps its field and its exact sentence. Read by src/ark-scene/aquatic-acts.ts.

clean_client.quote: A reef fish that earns safety by removing parasites and irritation from larger animals.
Juveniles set up cleaning stations and pick parasites from larger fish.

pair_patrol.quote: Adult pairs patrol a wide stretch of reef and hard bottom together, moving steadily from one feeding patch to the next.

clean_client.quote: It cleans algae off the shells of green sea turtles, which visit reef to be groomed.

mixed_follow.quote: Some morays cooperate with other predators such as groupers in reef hunting systems.
It is often reported feeding in mixed groups with other surgeonfishes over open ground rather than alone.
